d25891a054e2a009b4614d5c22ca1525835b40ed.6: Card HTTP endpoints have no tests, leaving routing, card-number masking, and access controls unverified for customers and staff. Ask the author to add endpoint tests covering permissions and responses.
d25891a054e2a009b4614d5c22ca1525835b40ed.7: The negative-amount payment test accepts any error, so real bugs could slip into production unnoticed. Ask the author to assert the exact expected validation error in that test.
d25891a054e2a009b4614d5c22ca1525835b40ed.8: Twelve changed methods, including card issuance, freeze, and unfreeze endpoints in CardsController, lack test evidence. Ask for test coverage proving customer actions and access rules behave safely.
d25891a054e2a009b4614d5c22ca1525835b40ed.9: Authorisation permissions block staff from approving payments and the automated test suite failed to run. Check that endpoint permissions are fixed and confirm all tests pass before signing.

7ea0adf51e98c0e654867901f4287de2a812930f.headline: Adds the term deposits module supporting opening, maturing, and breaking 3, 6, or 12-month fixed-rate deposits.
7ea0adf51e98c0e654867901f4287de2a812930f.summary: Introduces the Deposits module with domain entities, application service, API controller, database table, and DI registration. Customers can lock at least 500 in whole cents for 3, 6, or 12 months at fixed rates or break early without interest. Staff can mature deposits once due, transferring principal and rounded simple interest via the ledger.
7ea0adf51e98c0e654867901f4287de2a812930f.business: Customers can lock funds of at least 500 for 3, 6, or 12 months at 2.0%, 2.5%, or 3.0% annual interest, or break early to recover principal only. Staff trigger payouts after maturity.

b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.1: Staff cannot mature deposits and pay out customer funds because DepositsController stacks customer and staff permissions together. Ask the author to separate the policies per endpoint so staff-only access works.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.2: This change handles customer funds of 500 or more, fixed interest payouts, and early breaks. Verify the interest math, principal handling, and maturity payout rules against bank policy before signing off.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.3: Because DepositsController combines customer and staff access rules, staff cannot mature deposits for customers. Check the endpoint permissions and ask for the customer-level restriction to be moved to individual endpoints.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.4: Locking entries in DepositLocks are never cleaned up, which can slowly exhaust server memory and disrupt deposit services. Ask the author to add cleanup or a bounded cache for these locks.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.5: Uncleaned lock entries in DepositLocks pile up even for invalid deposit requests, risking server slowdown or downtime for customers. Ask the author to remove finished locks or bound the collection.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.6: DepositLocks keeps a lock in memory forever for every matured or broken deposit, risking outages over time. Ask how locks will be evicted once deposit processing finishes.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.7: DepositsController endpoints and access rules have no automated tests, leaving staff payouts and customer protections unverified. Ask for endpoint tests covering both allowed and forbidden user roles.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.8: Multi-currency deposits are untested, so interest payouts and holding accounts in non-EUR currencies could route money incorrectly. Ask for tests covering non-EUR deposits from opening through maturity and early break.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.9: There is no automated proof that only staff can trigger deposit payouts, risking unauthorized payouts or blocked operations. Ask for tests verifying that non-staff callers are rejected on maturity.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.10: Four DepositsController endpoints and constructor have no test evidence, meaning HTTP routing and access checks could fail in production. Ask for integration tests exercising all deposit endpoints.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.11: The HTTP layer in DepositsController blocks staff from maturing deposits unless they also hold customer access. Check how endpoint permissions match the requirement and ask for a fix and confirmation.
b73971b634a51a5600e7bea7494ee534a1ff5634.12: This is a high-risk financial change handling locked savings and interest payouts. Perform a full read of the deposit code and ensure two human sign-offs are recorded before merging.

309016bbd38eefdfe4c5686460c2a086c6e3501f.headline: Add Loans module for customer loan applications, annuity calculation, and officer approval or rejection.
309016bbd38eefdfe4c5686460c2a086c6e3501f.summary: Introduces the Bank.Modules.Loans module with API endpoints, application service logic, domain entity, and database persistence for fixed-rate loans. Customers can apply for and view their loans, while loan officers can inspect, approve, and reject applications with ledger disbursement and event notifications.
309016bbd38eefdfe4c5686460c2a086c6e3501f.business: Customers can apply for 6 to 120 month loans between 1000 and 50000 at a fixed 5.5% annual rate and receive decision notifications. Loan officers can review, approve with automatic principal disbursement to the customer account, or reject applications with a reason.

564d14bebf83e517d57613942e89449c4dbb2eae.13: The core four-eyes rule is missing in LoanService.ApproveAsync, letting officers approve their own loans and failing tests. Confirm this validation is added and all requirements pass before signing.
564d14bebf83e517d57613942e89449c4dbb2eae.14: Because this change carries high financial risk, a full human review of the code and two sign-offs are required. Ensure a second qualified reviewer signs off alongside you.

617defbe11201ca49acb33a958f1c95709376b47.headline: Enforce database uniqueness and per-key locking for idempotent payments
617defbe11201ca49acb33a958f1c95709376b47.summary: BankDbContext makes the composite index on Payment(CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) unique. PaymentService adds per-key and SQLite write semaphores, extracts execution into ExecuteIdempotentPaymentAsync with refreshed account state, and adds helpers to detach dirty entries and detect idempotency unique constraint violations.
617defbe11201ca49acb33a958f1c95709376b47.business: Customers retrying timed-out payments or sending concurrent identical requests with the same idempotency key are not charged twice and receive the original payment, while keys remain isolated per customer.

M:Bank.Data.BankDbContext.OnModelCreatin.changed: Marks the Payment composite index on CustomerId and IdempotencyKey as unique so the database rejects duplicate keys per customer.

F:Bank.Modules.Payments.Application.Paym.changed: Holds per-customer, per-idempotency-key semaphores to serialize concurrent payment requests sharing the same key.
Holds per-data-source semaphores to serialize writes across concurrent requests on file-based SQLite databases.
Weakly maps SQLite connections to write semaphores for in-memory or unnamed database connections.

M:Bank.Modules.Payments.Application.Paym.changed: Queries existing payments without tracking, serializes same-key requests using a key lock and SQLite write lock, and delegates to ExecuteIdempotentPaymentAsync.
Visible query body is unchanged, fetching a customer's payments ordered newest first.
Re-checks for an existing payment, refreshes account balance and overdraft state, computes FX and fees, and runs within a relational transaction.
Selects a connection- or file-scoped write lock when using relational SQLite without an active transaction.
Detaches all added, modified, and deleted entries from the database change tracker.
Checks SQLite error codes and exception messages to identify unique constraint failures on CustomerId and IdempotencyKey.

b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.0: Customers' payments stay stuck on hold even after money moves, causing reconciliation errors and failed-looking payments. Ask the author to mark the payment completed once transfers succeed and save that final state.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.1: Concurrent retries can crash with an unhandled error instead of returning the original payment while the first request is still finishing. Ask the author to wait or re-query after the winning transaction commits.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.2: Correct idempotency stops customers from being double-charged on mobile retries while keeping keys separate per customer. Verify that retries return the exact original payment without moving money twice.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.3: Storing per-key locks in memory forever will eventually crash the payment server and fails to block duplicates across multiple servers. Ask the author to remove the static lock dictionary and rely on database constraints.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.4: Embedding SQLite-specific locking inside PaymentService makes production database changes risky and harder for staff to maintain. Ask the author to remove provider-specific locks and let standard database transactions handle concurrency.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.5: Keeping a lock object for every payment key ever seen will slowly exhaust server memory and cause outages. Ask the author to remove this static dictionary or ensure entries are reliably evicted.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.6: Never cleaning up per-key locks in IdempotencyLocks will steadily consume memory until the payment service crashes. Ask the author to remove this in-memory cache or evict entries once processing finishes.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.7: Tying payment business logic to SQLite connection internals risks subtle failures when running on a real bank database. Ask the author to move concurrency control out of PaymentService into standard transaction handling.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.8: Caching a lock for every payment key without expiration will cause memory to grow until the service fails under traffic. Ask the author to remove the static cache or add strict eviction.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.9: Checking the database twice for the same existing payment slows down every payment and adds unnecessary database load. Ask the author to remove the duplicate lookup in PaymentService.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.10: Reading the customer's account balance twice in a row slows payments and adds needless database load. Ask the author to fetch the account balance and overdraft setting in a single query.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.11: Customers sending many unique idempotency keys could exhaust server memory and take down payments for everyone. Ask the author to remove the unbounded in-memory lock dictionary or enforce strict cleanup.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.12: The database index configuration and new SQLite locking paths lack passing test evidence, risking undetected production bugs. Ask the author to add and run tests covering these changed areas.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.13: Tests are currently failing, payments stay stuck on hold, and concurrent retries crash instead of returning the original payment. Do not approve until tests pass and both payment completion and concurrency handling are fixed.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.14: This high-risk payment change can directly impact customer money and double-charging protection. Perform a full line-by-line review and ensure two authorized reviewers sign off before merging.
b8ed10d9ef6b7c8fad5058a585171f31b64f1fab.15: Flaws in idempotency keys or memory growth could let attackers exhaust server memory or bypass duplicate-payment protections. Check that customer identity always comes from the authenticated user and memory cannot grow unboundedly.

6691c01e6f7ebf0578d8c007f9897f9610391e07.headline: Add compliance review workflow and endpoints for held payments
6691c01e6f7ebf0578d8c007f9897f9610391e07.summary: Adds a compliance review service, controller endpoints, and domain events to list, release, or reject held payments. Also injects customer notification support and a hold threshold into payment processing, alongside updated hold and reject transitions on the payment entity.
6691c01e6f7ebf0578d8c007f9897f9610391e07.business: Compliance officers gain dedicated endpoints to inspect held payments and release or reject others' payments with a mandatory rejection reason. Customers are notified during payment workflows, and payments reaching the hold threshold require compliance review before completion.

T:Bank.Modules.Payments.Api.RejectPaymen.changed: Adds request payload carrying an optional rejection reason string for rejecting a held payment.

T:Bank.Modules.Payments.Api.PaymentsCont.changed: Injects the payment review service and exposes compliance-only endpoints to list, release, and reject held payments.

b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.0: Compliance staff without customer permissions will be blocked with 403 errors on held, release, and reject endpoints. Ask the author to fix the authorization policy on PaymentsController.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.1: Releasing a held payment debits the customer account a second time instead of using the Suspense account. Ask the author to change ReleaseAsync to transfer funds from Suspense.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.2: Rejecting a held payment leaves the customer's money stranded in Suspense with no refund. Ask the author to add the Suspense-to-payer refund transfer in RejectAsync.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.3: Every payment is temporarily saved as held even when no review is needed, risking wrong statuses for customers if something fails. Ask the author to evaluate hold rules before calling Payment.Hold().
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.4: When a payment is held, money stays in the customer's account instead of moving to Suspense, so it could still be spent. Ask the author to transfer amount plus fee to Suspense upon hold.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.5: Releasing a held payment tries to debit the customer again while leaving money stuck in Suspense. Ask the author to update ReleaseAsync so it pays out from the Suspense account.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.6: Rejecting a held payment never returns sequestered funds from Suspense back to the customer. Ask the author to post the refund transfer in RejectAsync when a payment is rejected.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.7: Held payments skip reserving funds in Suspense, letting customers withdraw or spend money during compliance review. Ask the author to post the transfer to Suspense when a payment is held in PaymentService.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.8: This change adds high-impact fraud controls affecting customer notifications, compliance reviews, and money flows. Verify that compliance staff workflows, rejection reasons, and the 5,000 EUR hold threshold match bank policy.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.9: Compliance officers will get 403 errors because the controller requires both customer and compliance permissions together. Ask the author to separate compliance endpoints or remove the class-level customer restriction on PaymentsController.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.10: A lock entry is created for every payment and never removed, slowly leaking memory in long-running services. Ask the author to clean up or bound the PaymentLocks cache after review completes.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.11: Releasing a payment debits the customer's account directly instead of Suspense, risking double charges or failed payouts. Ask the author to source both amount and fee from Suspense in ReleaseAsync.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.12: Rejected payments change status without returning held money from Suspense, leaving customers out of pocket. Ask the author to refund amount plus fee from Suspense to the payer in RejectAsync.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.13: Held payments do not move money into Suspense, breaking the bank's fraud-hold protection. Ask the author to transfer amount plus fee from the payer to Suspense whenever a payment is held.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.14: Reading the request body manually bypasses standard validation and adds unnecessary maintenance risk for staff. Ask the author to replace ReadOptionalJsonBodyAsync with standard ASP.NET Core model binding.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.15: Normal payments are briefly stored as held before checking the rules, distorting payment history and adding database load. Ask the author to only transition status to held after confirming hold criteria apply.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.16: Storing a permanent lock object per reviewed payment will steadily consume server memory over time. Ask the author to remove entries after use or use a bounded locking mechanism in PaymentLocks.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.17: Compliance staff cannot access review endpoints unless they also hold a customer role, blocking fraud operations. Ask the author to ensure Held, Release, and Reject on PaymentsController do not require the Customer policy.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.18: Retaining a lock entry forever for every reviewed payment causes unbounded memory growth in PaymentReviewService. Ask the author to clean up or bound PaymentLocks so production stability is not affected.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.19: There are no tests checking whether large payments to new payees are actually held or routed to Suspense. Ask the author to add PaymentService.PayAsync tests covering hold thresholds, repeat payees, and Suspense transfers.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.20: Happy paths for releasing and rejecting held payments are untested, leaving fund transfers and notifications unverified. Ask the author to add tests in FraudHoldTests confirming Suspense payouts, refunds, statuses, and events.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.21: Self-approval blocks and invalid-status checks lack tests, risking compliance officers releasing their own payments or non-held payments. Ask the author to add negative tests for these rules in FraudHoldTests.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.22: Thirteen changed methods, including PaymentsController endpoints, lack usable test evidence, leaving edge cases unverified before release. Check which controller and service paths still need automated tests before signing off.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.23: Core Suspense accounting and hold sequencing are broken, putting customer balances and fraud stops at risk. Ask the author to fix Suspense transfers on hold, release, and reject, and only hold qualifying payments.
b14ee12de4ccafb0130f4a7bebbf1b220723640c.24: Because this change touches high-risk payment flows and compliance controls, a full code read and two sign-offs are required. Check that all critical accounting and authorization fixes are completed before approving.
